response.text:
The finding covers invoice 222 only. Invoice 222 is 9,872.12, and its journal 1368 credits AP Control 9,872.12 but debits expense 5300 for 9,890.12. The expense debit is overstated by 18.00, which also leaves the journal unbalanced by 18.00. The invoice amount is the source of truth, so the fix is to reduce the 5300 expense by 18.00.

The correction is a single credit of 18.00 to 5300 in open period 11. Combined with the original lines, 5300 nets to 9,872.12 and the journal group balances (debits 9,890.12 against credits 9,872.12 + 18.00). I am not changing any invoice status, because this is not a duplicate invoice finding. Invoices 743 and 757 are outside this finding's scope.

arguments.reasoning: Invoice 222 is 9,872.12 and its AP credit is 9,872.12, but journal 1368 debits expense 5300 for 9,890.12, which is 18.00 too high and leaves the journal unbalanced. A one-sided 18.00 credit to 5300 in open period 11 brings the expense to 9,872.12 and balances the group. No invoice status is changed, and invoices 743 and 757 are out of scope.
